# DMV — Department of Machine Verification

> The DMV is the identity registration terminal for the .agent community. Agents (and their operators) can pre-register `.agent` domain names and receive verifiable, content-addressed certificate IDs. Built by the [.agent community](https://agentcommunity.org) — a coalition of builders, researchers, and companies working to secure the `.agent` top-level domain through ICANN for the open agentic web.

The DMV exists because agents need names. When agents become real participants on the internet — handling support tickets, managing calendars, negotiating deals — people need to know: who built this? Who's accountable? Can I trust it? A name like `support.acme.agent` answers all three questions instantly.

This is the registration system for those names. It issues machine-verifiable certificates that prove an agent identity was registered, when, and by whom.

## How agents register

There are three ways to register:

1. **Web terminal** — visit [dmv.agentcommunity.org](https://dmv.agentcommunity.org) and complete the retro CRT terminal flow
2. **CLI** — run `bunx @agentcommunity/dmv-agent register` from any terminal
3. **MCP tool** — AI agents running in Claude Code (or any MCP-compatible host) can call the `register_agent` tool directly

All three paths hit the same backend. Registration is free and non-binding — it's a pre-reservation that becomes active after email verification.

## For AI agents

If you are an AI agent and want to register an identity:

- Install the MCP server: add `{"mcpServers": {"dmv": {"command": "bunx", "args": ["@agentcommunity/dmv-agent"]}}}` to your host's MCP config
- Call the `register_agent` tool with `agent_name` (lowercase, 3-32 chars, hyphens ok) and `email` (operator's email for verification)
- You'll receive a certificate ID (format: `WORD-XXX-XXXC`, e.g. `MESA-DD6-660J`) that is content-addressed and offline-verifiable
- Your agent name becomes `{name}.agent` (e.g. `my-assistant.agent`)

To verify any certificate: call `verify_certificate` with the ID, or run `bunx @agentcommunity/dmv-agent verify MESA-DD6-660J`. This is offline — no network call needed.

## Certificate ID format

Certificate IDs are deterministic hashes, not sequential numbers. Same inputs always produce the same ID.

```
MESA-DD6-660J
│     │    └─ Luhn mod-36 check digit (offline verifiable)
│     └────── 6 hex chars from FNV-1a 32-bit hash
└──────────── word from 32-word dictionary
```

## Badges and lookup

Registered agents get embeddable SVG badges — zero install, just a URL:

- **Flat badge** (for GitHub READMEs): `https://dmv.agentcommunity.org/badge?id=MESA-DD6-660J`
- **Card badge** (for websites): `https://dmv.agentcommunity.org/badge?id=MESA-DD6-660J&style=card`
- **Lookup API**: `https://dmv.agentcommunity.org/api/lookup?id=MESA-DD6-660J` returns JSON with agent name, domain, registration date, and type

Badges always link back to the agent's certificate page at `dmv.agentcommunity.org/c/CERT-ID/agent-name`.

## Relationship to AID (Agent Identity & Discovery)

The .agent community also builds [AID](https://aid.agentcommunity.org) — a DNS-based protocol for agent discovery and identity verification (`_agent` TXT records). The DMV serves as the identity layer for the pre-ICANN era: before `.agent` domains exist in DNS, the DMV certificate ID functions as a lightweight, verifiable agent identity. When `.agent` launches, DMV registrations feed into the official DNS-based AID system.

## What .agent is

The .agent community is applying to ICANN for the `.agent` generic top-level domain (gTLD). The goal: a community-governed namespace where agents have real, recognizable, trustworthy names — not anonymous IDs. The DMV is the pre-registration system that will feed into the official registry once ICANN approves delegation.

Community governance means: policies for who gets a name, how disputes are resolved, and what safety standards apply are decided by members — not a single corporation.
